title: NY State Senate · District 34
area: Northeast Bronx (Co-op City, Pelham Bay, Throggs Neck, City Island) and parts of southern Westchester County (Pelham, Pelham Manor).

context.text: Both major-party primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent Nathalia Fernandez advanced on the Democratic and Working Families lines and Adrian Romero advanced on the Conservative line without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Nathalia Fernandez
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 34 (since January 2023)

summary.text: Nathalia Fernandez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 34, which covers the east Bronx and part of southern Westchester County. A former legislative aide and staff member in the office of Governor Andrew Cuomo, she won a 2018 special election to the State Assembly, represented Assembly District 80 until 2023, and has been a state senator since January 2023. She chairs the Senate Alcoholism and Substance Use Disorders Committee.

background.text: According to Wikipedia, she was born in 1988 to a father who immigrated from Cuba and a mother who immigrated from Colombia, grew up in Rockland and then Westchester County, and graduated from North Salem High School. In her 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a daughter of immigrants whose father started and ran a small business.
Earned a B.A. in public relations from Hofstra University in 2010.
Worked as an administrative assistant at Genesis Realty Group and as an executive coordinator and chief of staff to Assemblymember Mark Gjonaj before running for office.
Served as a Bronx regional representative in the office of Governor Andrew Cuomo; Wikipedia dates her start in that role to 2017.

Won an April 24, 2018 special election for the 80th Assembly District, the seat vacated by Mark Gjonaj after he won a New York City Council seat, defeating Republican Gene DeFrancis. She was re-elected in 2018 and 2020 and represented the district until moving to the State Senate.

In 2022 she said she co-chaired the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus's Subcommittee on Minority and Women-Owned Enterprise & Economic Development and had passed the Andrew Kearse Act, which requires that people in police custody be given medical attention if needed.
Took office in the State Senate on January 1, 2023, succeeding Alessandra Biaggi. The nysenate.gov biography describes her as the first Latina to represent the 34th Senate District.

Chairs the Senate Alcoholism and Substance Use Disorders Committee and co-chairs the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction and Overdose Prevention; her other committee assignments include Agriculture, Cannabis, Insurance, Labor, Mental Health, Rules and Transportation.
Her Bronx Times profile (2022) listed her residence as Morris Park.

priorities.text: "I want to build resiliency for our coastal communities, increase transit access, funding for our schools and bring good paying jobs to uplift our local economy."

"Climate change is a constant concern for this area. Our coastal communities are threatened and our roads and transit systems often flood. We need to build long term resilience for this district through investing in infrastructure that stays strong against climate change and providing homeowners with assistance to protect their property."
"The East Bronx is a transportation desert... I want to make that a reality. We need transit access to connect our communities and continue to build economic growth for the area."

"I have a history of championing small businesses... I will do this through addressing the high property taxes that are getting in the way of their growth and honor the diversity of this district through uplifting minority and women owned businesses."

record.text: Sponsored S10156-B, establishing a school speed-zone camera demonstration program in the Village of Pelham; signed by the Governor August 14, 2026 (Chapter 216).

Sponsored S10632, which would prohibit a victim's voluntary intoxication from being used as a defense to a sex-crime charge; passed the Senate 60–0 on June 4, 2026 and remained in the Assembly Codes Committee.
Sponsored S10149, which would remove preauthorization requirements for outpatient substance use disorder treatment coverage; in Senate Insurance Committee as of April 30, 2026.

candidates.name: Adrian Romero
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced to the general election on the Conservative Party line without appearing on a primary ballot; did not appear on the Republican primary ballot.

summary.text: Adrian Romero is running for New York State Senate District 34 on the Conservative Party line against incumbent Nathalia Fernandez. Public sources found for this guide give little biographical detail beyond his candidacy and party endorsement.

background.text: Endorsed by the Bronx County Conservative Party as part of its slate of 2026 Republican candidates.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey were found for Adrian Romero as of 2026-09-25 (checked https://ballotpedia.org/Adrian_Romero, which has no Biography section). A Branch.vote candidate profile (checked 2026-09-25) likewise reported no platform information as of April 2026, and his campaign Facebook page (facebook.com/voteadrianromero) has only slogans and hashtags, no policy statements. His personal Facebook page name indicates he works as a real estate agent, and a Bronx County Conservative Party endorsement post names him among its 2026 endorsees, but neither contains his own statements on policy, so no priorities or positions were added. Re-searched 2026-10-19; still no website or first-person statements.
